outcome: branch (d) neither passes: the prune cost does not depend on which expert is removed - it is intrinsic to removing one at all, and the controller's choice is not a lever
summary_note: Section 5.31. All three policies run on the same seed, initial model and data schedule with every event forced to a prune, and all three remove the same NUMBER of experts from the same layer, so they differ only in which identities survive. Both primaries are on the FUSED loss, signed so a win is the primary's prediction: fused(Q) - fused(R) < 0 and fused(R) - fused(B) < 0. The penalty own - fused is reported as a mechanism secondary and is not verdict-bearing, because it is a difference between two processes and a policy that leaves a harder-to-retrain topology shows a smaller penalty even when its own fused run is worse.
